summary.prose: Building s1 lays the shared groundwork for a multi-threaded daemon without moving any request off the main thread yet. It first pins, as a test, that a worker thread can open LMDB without dropping the daemon's lock, then adds the shared-memory store guard, the main-thread hub with its registry and status board, process-wide store health, and strong cross-thread reads for Lance with DuckDB behind one permit. Finally the four MCP step-state stores move onto the hub, which turns about 48 call sites async, and cross-thread tests prove the Story's acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Gating test: a worker thread's LMDB open, use and release keeps the daemon's lock
tasks.summary: Turn the 2026-10-21 simulation into a committed integration test on a temporary store with the production open options: the main thread opens; a real worker_thread opens, reads, writes, closes and exits; another process opens and closes; a lock probe reports the lock held at each step and the main thread's next write succeeds. A positive control (closing a stray descriptor on the lock file) proves the probe can see a dropped lock. This is the Story's gate: if it fails, the Story stops and the question goes back to the HLD before any later task.
acceptanceChecks: The test passes with the lock held after every step, including worker exit and another process's open/close.
The positive control reports the lock dropped, so a probe that always says held would fail the test.

tests.name: a worker thread's LMDB open, read, write, close and exit keep the daemon's lock, and the main thread writes after another process opens and closes the store
the lock probe reports a dropped lock after a stray descriptor on the lock file is closed

tasks.title: Store guard: shared-memory permits, async-chain nesting, per-acquisition holders, reclaim
tasks.summary: Add the process-wide StoreGuardBlock (permit counters, per-acquisition holder records, the store health word) and withStore, policy, holders, reclaim and quiescence with the initial policy table (graph and lance direct, duckdb guarded with one permit). Waiting is asynchronous with a time limit and abort signal; release runs in a finally; nesting is refused per async call chain with an async-context marker; concurrent same-thread calls queue in arrival order.
acceptanceChecks: withStore releases on resolve, reject, synchronous throw and abort.
Two concurrent same-thread withStore('duckdb') calls both complete one after the other; withStore from inside a held op fails with StoreLockNestedError.
An acquisition past its limit fails with StoreLockTimeoutError naming the holder.
reclaim releases a terminated worker's permits after quiescence and marks a store unhealthy past limitMs.

tests.name: withStore releases its permit on resolve, reject, synchronous throw and abort
an acquisition past its limit fails with StoreLockTimeoutError naming the holder
two concurrent same-thread withStore calls on a one-permit store both complete in turn; withStore inside a held op fails with StoreLockNestedError
reclaim releases after quiescence and marks the store unhealthy past limitMs
a worker terminated while holding a permit has it reclaimed and another worker then acquires it

tasks.title: Thread channel and hub client
tasks.summary: Add the ChannelEnvelope types, the hub request/reply protocol and the worker-side hub client, whose pending requests fail with HubUnavailableError when the port closes.
acceptanceChecks: A worker's hub request is answered with the matching requestId.
A closed port rejects every pending request with HubUnavailableError; no request hangs.

tests.name: a worker's hub request is answered with its own requestId
closing the port rejects every pending hub request with HubUnavailableError

tasks.title: Target registry and status board
tasks.summary: Add the main-thread TargetRegistry (register, unregister, targetFor with the unattributed target) and the StatusBoard (publish, publishIndexing, publishClients, publishRun, publishStore, snapshot), reachable from workers through the hub.
acceptanceChecks: register/unregister/targetFor follow the conflict rules; a re-register after unregister succeeds; an unknown unregister is a no-op.
Each publish* is reflected in snapshot (latest per thread, runs by runId with frames only growing); an empty board snapshots as specified; a worker's publish appears in a main-thread snapshot.

tests.name: TargetRegistry refuses a second live admin, indexing, unattributed or same-session target and resolves an identity-less session request to the unattributed target
a target re-registered after unregister succeeds and unregistering an unknown thread is a no-op
StatusBoard keeps the latest status per thread and snapshots empty as specified
publishIndexing, publishClients, publishRun and publishStore are each reflected in snapshot, runs by runId with frames only growing
a status published from a worker appears in a main-thread snapshot

tasks.title: Process-wide store health
tasks.summary: Make every reader of the graph store's health (getStoreHealth, recordLocksLost, getGraphStore, withWriteTxn, withWriteTxnSync, runReaderCheck, closeGraphStore) read the shared health word; recordLocksLost sets it with a compare-and-swap and publishes the full record through the hub so every thread keeps a copy.
acceptanceChecks: Locks-lost recorded in a worker makes the main thread's next getGraphStore and withWriteTxn fail with LmdbStoreLocksLostError and write nothing.
runReaderCheck stops probing and closeGraphStore skips the library close in every thread; only the first detection logs.

tests.name: locks-lost recorded in a worker makes the main thread's next getGraphStore and withWriteTxn fail with LmdbStoreLocksLostError and write nothing
after locks-lost in a worker, getStoreHealth on the main thread reports it, runReaderCheck does not probe and a second detection does not log

tasks.title: Lance strong read consistency and DuckDB behind the guard
tasks.summary: Open Lance with readConsistencyInterval 0 and route DuckDB's withConnection through withStore('duckdb') so one 2 GB budget is shared; keep every existing behaviour.
acceptanceChecks: A Lance write in one thread is read from another; with the interval unset the same read misses it.
Two threads' DuckDB queries run one after the other and both succeed.

tests.name: a Lance write in one thread is read from another with readConsistencyInterval 0 and missed with it unset
two threads' DuckDB queries run one after the other behind the one permit and both succeed

tasks.title: Shared step-state store on the hub
tasks.summary: Host the four step kinds on the hub behind SharedStepStateStore with per-kind lifecycle adapters (100-entry LRU, 1-hour TTL, read refresh; rotate-token for analyze and workflow, stable-token for review, consume-per-stage for code-review) and a structured-clone check per kind.
acceptanceChecks: Each kind's token rule, eviction, TTL and read refresh behave as today's store.
A real payload of each kind survives a structured clone; state minted in one worker is read in another after the first exits.

tests.name: each step kind's token rule, 100-entry eviction, TTL with read refresh and release match today's stores
a real payload of each step kind survives a structured clone through the hub
step state minted in one worker is read in another after the first exits

tasks.title: Analyze and workflow step callers move to the async shared store
tasks.summary: Switch the analyze-step and workflow-step state-store modules and their encode/reencode/decode wrappers to the async shared store, add await at their call sites (analyze-step state.ts and phases start, plan, narrow, bundle; workflow-step state.ts and phases start, plan, step, synthesize), and make their test-only helpers async for their test files.
acceptanceChecks: Every analyze and workflow call site awaits the async API; tsc is clean.
The analyze-step and workflow-step suites, including analyze-step-state.test.ts and workflow-step/__tests__/state-store.test.ts, pass unchanged in meaning with today's not-found messages.

tests.name: src/daemon/steps/__tests__/analyze-step-state.test.ts passes unchanged in meaning against the hub-backed store
src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/__tests__/state-store.test.ts passes unchanged in meaning, with today's not-found messages

tasks.title: Review and code-review step callers move to the async shared store
tasks.summary: Switch the review-step and code-review-step state-store modules to the async shared store, add await at their call sites (review-step phases start, claims, findings, verdicts; code-review-step handler), and make their test-only helpers async for their test files, including the code-review attribution tests.
acceptanceChecks: Every review and code-review call site awaits the async API; tsc is clean.

The review-step and code-review-step suites, peer-state-store-leakfree.test.ts, code-review-rpc-fallback.test.ts and the code-review attribution tests pass unchanged in meaning; a superseded code-review token still fails.

tests.name: src/daemon/steps/__tests__/peer-state-store-leakfree.test.ts passes unchanged in meaning against the hub-backed stores
a superseded code-review token fails with today's not-found message
src/daemon/__tests__/code-review-rpc-fallback.test.ts passes unchanged in meaning

tasks.title: Worker store ownership and the cross-thread store tests
tasks.summary: Make declareLiveStoreOwner part of the worker entry (client processes still refused) and add the acceptance tests: concurrent writer/reader on two threads, two threads' writes read by a third, a throwing transaction on a worker leaving nothing visible, and non-owner refusal.
acceptanceChecks: ac1: a reader on one thread sees only whole transactions while another writes, and vectors never precede their graph row.
ac2: two threads' artifact and config writes are read back from a third.
ac3: a non-owner worker is refused on the live paths.
ac4: a throwing transaction on a worker leaves nothing visible.

tests.name: a reader on one thread sees only whole LMDB transactions while a worker writes, and vectors never precede their graph row
two workers' artifact-vector and config writes are read back from a third thread
a worker that has not declared the store owner is refused on the live LMDB and Lance paths
no module outside src/daemon and src/db calls declareLiveStoreOwner
a throwing withWriteTxn callback on a worker leaves none of its writes visible to the main thread
